verses.original: Καὶ διασωθέντες τότε ἐπέγνωμεν ὅτι Μελίτη ἡ νῆσος καλεῖται
verses.transliteration: Kai diasōthentes tote epegnōmen hoti Melitē hē nēsos kaleitai
verses.literal: Once we were safely ashore we learned that the island was called Malta
verses.literalPt: E, HAVENDO escapado, então souberam que a ilha se chamava Malta.

verses.original: οἵ τε βάρβαροι παρεῖχον οὐ τὴν τυχοῦσαν φιλανθρωπίαν ἡμῖν ἅψαντες γὰρ πυρὰν προσελάβοντο πάντας ἡμᾶς διὰ τὸν ὑετὸν τὸν ἐφεστῶτα καὶ διὰ τὸ ψῦχος
verses.transliteration: hoi te barbaroi pareichon ou tēn tychousan philanthrōpian hēmin hapsantes gar pyran proselabonto pantas hēmas dia ton hyeton ton ephestōta kai dia to psychos
verses.literal: The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness They kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining - and - cold
verses.literalPt: E os bárbaros usaram conosco de não pouca humanidade; porque, acendendo uma grande fogueira, nos recolheram a todos por causa da chuva que caía, e por causa do frio.

verses.original: Συστρέψαντος δὲ τοῦ Παύλου φρυγάνων τι πλῆθος καὶ ἐπιθέντος ἐπὶ τὴν πυράν ἔχιδνα ἀπὸ τῆς θέρμης ἐξελθοῦσα καθῆψεν τῆς χειρὸς αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Systrepsantos de tou Paulou phryganōn ti plēthos kai epithentos epi tēn pyran echidna apo tēs thermēs exelthousa kathēpsen tēs cheiros autou
verses.literal: Paul gathered a bundle of sticks and as he laid them on the fire a viper driven out by the heat fastened itself to his hand
verses.literalPt: E, havendo Paulo ajuntado uma quantidade de vides, e pondo-as no fogo, uma víbora, fugindo do calor, lhe acometeu a mão.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ εἶδον οἱ βάρβαροι κρεμάμενον τὸ θηρίον ἐκ τῆς χειρὸς αὐτοῦ πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἔλεγον Πάντως φονεύς ἐστιν ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος ὃν διασωθέντα ἐκ τῆς θαλάσσης ἡ Δίκη ζῆν οὐκ εἴασεν
verses.transliteration: hōs de eidon hoi barbaroi kremamenon to thērion ek tēs cheiros autou pros allēlous elegon Pantōs phoneus estin ho anthrōpos houtos hon diasōthenta ek tēs thalassēs hē Dikē zēn ouk eiasen
verses.literal: When the islanders saw the creature hanging from his hand they said to one another Surely this man is a murderer Although he was saved from the sea Justice has not allowed him to live
verses.literalPt: E os bárbaros, vendo-lhe a víbora pendurada na mão, diziam uns aos outros: Certamente este homem é homicida, visto como, escapando do mar, a justiça não o deixa viver.

verses.original: ὁ μὲν οὖν ἀποτινάξας τὸ θηρίον εἰς τὸ πῦρ ἔπαθεν οὐδὲν κακόν
verses.transliteration: ho men oun apotinaxas to thērion eis to pyr epathen ouden kakon
verses.literal: But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects
verses.literalPt: Mas, sacudindo ele a víbora no fogo, não sofreu nenhum mal.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ προσεδόκων αὐτὸν μέλλειν πίμπρασθαι ἢ καταπίπτειν ἄφνω νεκρόν ἐπὶ πολὺ δὲ αὐτῶν προσδοκώντων καὶ θεωρούντων μηδὲν ἄτοπον εἰς αὐτὸν γινόμενον μεταβαλόμενοι ἔλεγον αὐτὸν εἶναι θεόν
verses.transliteration: hoi de prosedokōn auton mellein pimprasthai ē katapiptein aphnō nekron epi poly de autōn prosdokōntōn kai theōrountōn mēden atopon eis auton ginomenon metabalomenoi elegon auton einai theon
verses.literal: The islanders were expecting him to swell up or suddenly drop dead But after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him they changed their minds and said he was a god
verses.literalPt: E eles esperavam que viesse a inchar ou a cair morto de repente; mas tendo esperado já muito, e vendo que nenhum incômodo lhe sobrevinha, mudando de parecer, diziam que era um deus.

verses.original: Ἐν δὲ τοῖς περὶ τὸν τόπον ἐκεῖνον ὑπῆρχεν χωρία τῷ πρώτῳ τῆς νήσου ὀνόματι Ποπλίῳ ὃς ἀναδεξάμενος ἡμᾶς ἡμέρας τρεῖς φιλοφρόνως ἐξένισεν
verses.transliteration: En de tois peri ton topon ekeinon hypērchen chōria tō prōtō tēs nēsou onomati Popliō hos anadexamenos hēmas hēmeras treis philophronōs exenisen
verses.literal: Nearby . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . stood an estate belonging to Publius the chief official of the island He welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days
verses.literalPt: E ali, próximo daquele lugar, havia umas herdades que pertenciam ao principal da ilha, por nome Públio, o qual nos recebeu e hospedou benignamente por três dias.

verses.original: ἐγένετο δὲ τὸν πατέρα τοῦ Ποπλίου πυρετοῖς καὶ δυσεντερίῳ συνεχόμενον κατακεῖσθαι πρὸς ὃν ὁ Παῦλος εἰσελθὼν καὶ προσευξάμενος ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῷ ἰάσατο αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: egeneto de ton patera tou Popliou pyretois kai dysenteriō synechomenon katakeisthai pros hon ho Paulos eiselthōn kai proseuxamenos epitheis tas cheiras autō iasato auton
verses.literal: The father of Publius was sick in bed suffering from fever and dysentery Paul went in to see him and after praying and placing his hands on him he healed the man
verses.literalPt: E aconteceu estar de cama enfermo de febre e disenteria o pai de Públio, que Paulo foi ver, e, havendo orado, pôs as mãos sobre ele, e o curou.

verses.original: τούτου δὲ γενομένου καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ οἱ ἐν τῇ νήσῳ ἔχοντες ἀσθενείας προσήρχοντο καὶ ἐθεραπεύοντο
verses.transliteration: toutou de genomenou kai hoi loipoi hoi en tē nēsō echontes astheneias prosērchonto kai etherapeuonto
verses.literal: After this had happened the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured as well
verses.literalPt: Feito, pois, isto, vieram também ter com ele os demais que na ilha tinham enfermidades, e sararam.

verses.original: οἳ καὶ πολλαῖς τιμαῖς ἐτίμησαν ἡμᾶς καὶ ἀναγομένοις ἐπέθεντο τὰ πρὸς τὰς χρείας
verses.transliteration: hoi kai pollais timais etimēsan hēmas kai anagomenois epethento ta pros tas chreias
verses.literal: The islanders honored us in many ways and supplied - our needs when we were ready to sail
verses.literalPt: Os quais nos distinguiram também com muitas honras; e, havendo de navegar, nos proveram das coisas necessárias.

verses.original: Μετὰ δὲ τρεῖς μῆνας ἀνήχθημεν ἐν πλοίῳ παρακεχειμακότι ἐν τῇ νήσῳ Ἀλεξανδρινῷ παρασήμῳ Διοσκούροις
verses.transliteration: Meta de treis mēnas anēchthēmen en ploiō parakecheimakoti en tē nēsō Alexandrinō parasēmō Dioskourois
verses.literal: After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island It had the Twin Brothers as a figurehead
verses.literalPt: E três meses depois partimos num navio de Alexandria que invernara na ilha, o qual tinha por insígnia Castor e Pólux.

verses.original: καὶ καταχθέντες εἰς Συρακούσας ἐπεμείναμεν ἡμέρας τρεῖς
verses.transliteration: kai katachthentes eis Syrakousas epemeinamen hēmeras treis
verses.literal: Putting in at Syracuse we stayed there three days
verses.literalPt: E, chegando a Siracusa, ficamos ali três dias.

verses.original: ὅθεν περιελόντες κατηντήσαμεν εἰς Ῥήγιον καὶ μετὰ μίαν ἡμέραν ἐπιγενομένου νότου δευτεραῖοι ἤλθομεν εἰς Ποτιόλους
verses.transliteration: hothen perielontes katēntēsamen eis Rhēgion kai meta mian hēmeran epigenomenou notou deuteraioi ēlthomen eis Potiolous
verses.literal: From there we weighed anchor and came to Rhegium After one day a south wind came up and on the second day we arrived at Puteoli
verses.literalPt: De onde, indo costeando, viemos a Régio; e soprando, um dia depois, um vento do sul, chegamos no segundo dia a Potéoli.

verses.original: οὗ εὑρόντες ἀδελφοὺς παρεκλήθημεν παρ’ αὐτοῖς ἐπιμεῖναι ἡμέρας ἑπτά καὶ οὕτως εἰς τὴν Ῥώμην ἤλθαμεν
verses.transliteration: hou heurontes adelphous pareklēthēmen par’ autois epimeinai hēmeras hepta kai houtōs eis tēn Rhōmēn ēlthamen
verses.literal: There we found some brothers who invited us to spend the week . . . with them And so we came to Rome
verses.literalPt: Onde, achando alguns irmãos, nos rogaram que por sete dias ficássemos com eles; e depois nos dirigimos a Roma.

verses.original: Κἀκεῖθεν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ ἀκούσαντες τὰ περὶ ἡμῶν ἦλθαν εἰς ἀπάντησιν ἡμῖν ἄχρι Ἀππίου Φόρου καὶ Τριῶν Ταβερνῶν οὓς ἰδὼν ὁ Παῦλος εὐχαριστήσας τῷ Θεῷ ἔλαβε θάρσος
verses.transliteration: Kakeithen hoi adelphoi akousantes ta peri hēmōn ēlthan eis apantēsin hēmin achri Appiou Phorou kai Triōn Tabernōn hous idōn ho Paulos eucharistēsas tō Theō elabe tharsos
verses.literal: The brothers there had heard about us and traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us When Paul saw them he was encouraged and gave thanks to God
verses.literalPt: E de lá, ouvindo os irmãos novas de nós, nos saíram ao encontro à Praça de Ápio e às Três Vendas, e Paulo, vendo-os, deu graças a Deus e tomou ânimo.

verses.original: Ὅτε δὲ εἰσήλθομεν εἰς Ῥώμην ἐπετράπη τῷ Παύλῳ μένειν καθ’ ἑαυτὸν σὺν τῷ φυλάσσοντι αὐτὸν στρατιώτῃ
verses.transliteration: Hote de eisēlthomen eis Rhōmēn epetrapē tō Paulō menein kath’ heauton syn tō phylassonti auton stratiōtē
verses.literal: When we arrived in Rome Paul was permitted to stay by himself with a soldier to guard him
verses.literalPt: E, logo que chegamos a Roma, o centurião entregou os presos ao capitão da guarda; mas a Paulo se lhe permitiu morar por sua conta à parte, com o soldado que o guardava.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ ἡμέρας τρεῖς συνκαλέσασθαι αὐτὸν τοὺς ὄντας τῶν Ἰουδαίων πρώτους συνελθόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἔλεγεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ἐγώ ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί οὐδὲν ἐναντίον ποιήσας τῷ λαῷ ἢ τοῖς ἔθεσι τοῖς πατρῴοις δέσμιος ἐξ Ἱεροσολύμων παρεδόθην εἰς τὰς χεῖρας τῶν Ῥωμαίων
verses.transliteration: Egeneto de meta hēmeras treis synkalesasthai auton tous ontas tōn Ioudaiōn prōtous synelthontōn de autōn elegen pros autous Egō andres adelphoi ouden enantion poiēsas tō laō ē tois ethesi tois patrōois desmios ex Hierosolymōn paredothēn eis tas cheiras tōn Rhōmaiōn
verses.literal: After three days he called together the leaders of the Jews When they had gathered he said to them Brothers although I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers I was taken prisoner in Jerusalem and handed over to - the Romans
verses.literalPt: E aconteceu que, três dias depois, Paulo convocou os principais dos judeus e, juntos eles, lhes disse: Homens irmãos, não havendo eu feito nada contra o povo, ou contra os ritos paternos, vim contudo preso desde Jerusalém, entregue nas mãos dos romanos;

verses.original: οἵτινες ἀνακρίναντές με ἐβούλοντο ἀπολῦσαι διὰ τὸ μηδεμίαν αἰτίαν θανάτου ὑπάρχειν ἐν ἐμοί
verses.transliteration: hoitines anakrinantes me eboulonto apolysai dia to mēdemian aitian thanatou hyparchein en emoi
verses.literal: They examined me and wanted to release me because there was no basis for a death sentence against me
verses.literalPt: Os quais, havendo-me examinado, queriam soltar-me, por não haver em mim crime algum de morte.

verses.original: ἀντιλεγόντων δὲ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἠναγκάσθην ἐπικαλέσασθαι Καίσαρα οὐχ ὡς τοῦ ἔθνους μου ἔχων τι κατηγορεῖν
verses.transliteration: antilegontōn de tōn Ioudaiōn ēnankasthēn epikalesasthai Kaisara ouch hōs tou ethnous mou echōn ti katēgorein
verses.literal: But when the Jews objected I was compelled to appeal to Caesar even though I have no charge to bring against my nation
verses.literalPt: Mas, opondo-se os judeus, foi-me forçoso apelar para César, não tendo, contudo, de que acusar a minha nação.

verses.original: διὰ ταύτην οὖν τὴν αἰτίαν παρεκάλεσα ὑμᾶς ἰδεῖν καὶ προσλαλῆσαι ἕνεκεν γὰρ τῆς ἐλπίδος τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ τὴν ἅλυσιν ταύτην περίκειμαι
verses.transliteration: dia tautēn oun tēn aitian parekalesa hymas idein kai proslalēsai heneken gar tēs elpidos tou Israēl tēn halysin tautēn perikeimai
verses.literal: So for this reason I have called to see you and speak with you It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain
verses.literalPt: Por esta causa vos chamei, para vos ver e falar; porque pela esperança de Israel estou com esta cadeia.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπαν Ἡμεῖς οὔτε γράμματα περὶ σοῦ ἐδεξάμεθα ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας οὔτε παραγενόμενός τις τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἀπήγγειλεν ἢ ἐλάλησέν τι περὶ σοῦ πονηρόν
verses.transliteration: Hoi de pros auton eipan Hēmeis oute grammata peri sou edexametha apo tēs Ioudaias oute paragenomenos tis tōn adelphōn apēngeilen ē elalēsen ti peri sou ponēron
verses.literal: The leaders replied - We have not received . . . any letters about you from Judea nor have any of the brothers from there reported or even mentioned anything bad about you
verses.literalPt: Então eles lhe disseram: Nós não recebemos acerca de ti carta alguma da Judéia, nem veio aqui algum dos irmãos, que nos anunciasse ou dissesse de ti mal algum.

verses.original: ἀξιοῦμεν δὲ παρὰ σοῦ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ φρονεῖς περὶ μὲν γὰρ τῆς αἱρέσεως ταύτης γνωστὸν ἡμῖν ἐστιν ὅτι πανταχοῦ ἀντιλέγεται
verses.transliteration: axioumen de para sou akousai ha phroneis peri men gar tēs haireseōs tautēs gnōston hēmin estin hoti pantachou antilegetai
verses.literal: But we consider your views worth hearing because - we know that people everywhere are speaking against this sect
verses.literalPt: No entanto bem quiséramos ouvir de ti o que sentes; porque, quanto a esta seita, notório nos é que em toda a parte se fala contra ela.

verses.original: Ταξάμενοι δὲ αὐτῷ ἡμέραν ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν ξενίαν πλείονες οἷς ἐξετίθετο διαμαρτυρόμενος τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ πείθων τε αὐτοὺς περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀπό τε τοῦ νόμου Μωϋσέως καὶ τῶν προφητῶν ἀπὸ πρωῒ ἕως ἑσπέρας
verses.transliteration: Taxamenoi de autō hēmeran ēlthon pros auton eis tēn xenian pleiones hois exetitheto diamartyromenos tēn basileian tou Theou peithōn te autous peri tou Iēsou apo te tou nomou Mōuseōs kai tōn prophētōn apo prōi heōs hesperas
verses.literal: So they set a day to meet with Paul and many people came to - the place he was staying He expounded to them from morning to evening testifying about the kingdom of God and persuading them about Jesus from the Law of Moses and the Prophets
verses.literalPt: E, havendo-lhe eles assinalado um dia, muitos foram ter com ele à pousada, aos quais declarava com bom testemunho o reino de Deus, e procurava persuadi-los à fé em Jesus, tanto pela lei de Moisés como pelos profetas, desde a manhã até à tarde.

verses.original: Καὶ οἱ μὲν ἐπείθοντο τοῖς λεγομένοις οἱ δὲ ἠπίστουν
verses.transliteration: Kai hoi men epeithonto tois legomenois hoi de ēpistoun
verses.literal: Some of them were convinced by what he said but others refused to believe
verses.literalPt: E alguns criam no que se dizia; mas outros não criam.

verses.original: ἀσύμφωνοι δὲ ὄντες πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἀπελύοντο εἰπόντος τοῦ Παύλου ῥῆμα ἓν ὅτι Καλῶς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον ἐλάλησεν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: asymphōnoi de ontes pros allēlous apelyonto eipontos tou Paulou rhēma hen hoti Kalōs to Pneuma to Hagion elalēsen dia Ēsaiou tou prophētou pros tous pateras hymōn
verses.literal: They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet
verses.literalPt: E, como ficaram entre si discordes, despediram-se, dizendo Paulo esta palavra: Bem falou o Espírito Santo a nossos pais pelo profeta Isaías,

verses.original: λέγων Πορεύθητι πρὸς τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον καὶ εἰπόν Ἀκοῇ ἀκούσετε καὶ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε καὶ βλέποντες βλέψετε καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδητε
verses.transliteration: legōn Poreuthēti pros ton laon touton kai eipon Akoē akousete kai ou mē synēte kai blepontes blepsete kai ou mē idēte
verses.literal: Go to this people and say You will be ever hearing . . . but never . . . understanding you will be ever seeing . . . but never . . . perceiving
verses.literalPt: Dizendo: Vai a este povo, e dize: De ouvido ouvireis, e de maneira nenhuma entendereis; E, vendo vereis, e de maneira nenhuma percebereis.

verses.original: ἐπαχύνθη γὰρ ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν βαρέως ἤκουσαν καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν ἐκάμμυσαν μή‿ ποτε ἴδωσιν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν ἀκούσωσιν καὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ συνῶσιν καὶ ἐπιστρέψωσιν καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: epachynthē gar hē kardia tou laou toutou kai tois ōsin bareōs ēkousan kai tous ophthalmous autōn ekammysan mē pote idōsin tois ophthalmois kai tois ōsin akousōsin kai tē kardia synōsin kai epistrepsōsin kai iasomai autous
verses.literal: For this people’s heart has grown callous they hardly hear . . . with their ears and they have closed their eyes Otherwise . . . they might see with their eyes hear with their ears understand with their hearts and turn and I would heal them
verses.literalPt: Porquanto o coração deste povo está endurecido, E com os ouvidos ouviram pesadamente, E fecharam os olhos, Para que nunca com os olhos vejam, Nem com os ouvidos ouçam, Nem do coração entendam, E se convertam, E eu os cure.

verses.original: Γνωστὸν οὖν ἔστω ὑμῖν ὅτι τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀπεστάλη τοῦτο τὸ σωτήριον τοῦ Θεοῦ αὐτοὶ καὶ ἀκούσονται
verses.transliteration: Gnōston oun estō hymin hoti tois ethnesin apestalē touto to sōtērion tou Theou autoi kai akousontai
verses.literal: Be advised therefore that - God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles and they will listen
verses.literalPt: Seja-vos, pois, notório que esta salvação de Deus é enviada aos gentios, e eles a ouvirão.
E, havendo ele dito estas palavras, partiram os judeus, tendo entre si grande contenda.

verses.original: Ἐνέμεινεν δὲ διετίαν ὅλην ἐν ἰδίῳ μισθώματι καὶ ἀπεδέχετο πάντας τοὺς εἰσπορευομένους πρὸς αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Enemeinen de dietian holēn en idiō misthōmati kai apedecheto pantas tous eisporeuomenous pros auton
verses.literal: Paul stayed there two full years . . . in his own rented house welcoming all who came to visit him
verses.literalPt: E Paulo ficou dois anos inteiros na sua própria habitação que alugara, e recebia todos quantos vinham vê-lo;

verses.original: κηρύσσων τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ διδάσκων τὰ περὶ τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ πάσης παρρησίας ἀκωλύτως
verses.transliteration: kēryssōn tēn basileian tou Theou kai didaskōn ta peri tou Kyriou Iēsou Christou meta pasēs parrēsias akōlytōs
verses.literal: Boldly and freely he proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ
verses.literalPt: Pregando o reino de Deus, e ensinando com toda a liberdade as coisas pertencentes ao Senhor Jesus Cristo, sem impedimento algum.
